## Best Miami airport hotels

【43†1. Hilton Miami Airport Blue Lagoon】

  * Hotels 
  * Allapattah

【43†Photograph: Courtesy Booking.com】

Airport hotels don't have to mean being surrounded by concrete. The Hilton Hotel is sat in the middle of a beautiful lagoon, that looks like a set from a Hollywood movie. The sleek spot caters to business travelers and vacationers alike with its spectacular vista, outdoor activities and functional workspaces.

Where is it? Four miles from the airport in leafy Blue Lagoon. Downtown Miami and Dolphin Mall are 15 minutes away.

Which room? Opt for a junior suite for extra space and stunning views. 

Time Out tip: Whether you’re used to sinking holes-in-one or have never picked up a putter before, you can surely wedge in nine holes at the Granada Golf Course. Opened in 1923, this historic course is among the oldest in the state. It’s also one of the best for beginners, with a fully stocked pro shop and no water hazards.  

【44†Check prices†www.booking.com】

【45†2. Pullman Miami Airport】

  * Hotels 
  * Blue Lagoon

【45†Photograph: Courtesy Booking.com】

Proof that the best Miami airport hotels offer more than just a decent night’s sleep, this convenient airport-adjacent hotel has much more flair than the standard options. In fact, to simply call the venue aesthetically pleasing would be an understatement, thanks to an interior laden with contemporary art and sophisticated furnishings and an exterior that evokes a sense of tropical grandeur.

Where is it? Just over 3 miles from the airport with a free shuttle service and minutes from Brickell City Centre, Downtown Miami, Port of Miami and beaches. 

Which room? Pick a lagoon side room for the best scenes from the window. 

Time Out tip: Traveling with family? The Pullman Miami Airport offers free accommodations and breakfast for up to two children under 12, so you can afford to bring the kids along on your next vacation. (We'll let you decide if that's good news or not).

【46†Check prices†www.booking.com】

Advertising

【47†3. Hyatt Regency Coral Gables in Miami】

  * Hotels 
  * Coral Gables

【47†Photograph: Courtesy Booking.com】

Old-world Spanish decor meets modern amenities in this charming Coral Gables hotel. At an easy distance from the strip, this airport hotel is not only good for those waiting for flights, but for those with an insatiable streak of Miami wanderlust, too.

Where is it? Six miles from downtown Miami in the heart of the fun-packed town of Coral Gables. 

Which room? We think the rooms with pool views really put the cherry on top if your stay. 

Time Out tip: No shade to the pool at the Hyatt Regency, but it just can’t compare to the crystal clear waters of the nearby Venetian Pool. The most gorgeous swimming hole in Coral Gables (if not the world) was once a coral rock quarry before it was turned into a full-service pool in the 1920s. Fed by a subterranean aquifer and flanked by palm trees, the freshwater pool looks impossibly idyllic. Since tourists descend on the pool over the weekend, you’ll want to visit on a weekday for a more serene swimming experience.

【48†Check prices†www.booking.com】

【49†4. Sheraton Miami Airport Hotel】

  * Hotels 
  * Miami

【49†Photograph: Courtesy Booking.com】

Don't let the humdrum exterior fool you, inside the Sheraton there’s some understated but impeccably stylish decor. But mostly, it's the proximity to an 18-hole golf course and an abundance of meeting rooms that make the Sheraton the perfect spot for business travelers.

Where is it? Little Havana and Marlins Park are on the doorstep. There’s also a free shuttle service runnig every 15 minutes 24-hours a day from the airport. 

Which room? The Traditional Rooms are easy on the wallet and offer great views and plenty of stylish amenities.  

Time Out tip: You can’t visit Little Havana without making a pilgrimage to Versailles, one of the city’s most iconic restaurants and a landmark in its own right. Ropa vieja, cubanos, seafood paella, flan: Versailles does all of it impeccably. Settle into a booth in the mirrored dining room, order up a Cuban feast and take in the ambiance—you won’t find anything like it anywhere else.

【50†Check prices†www.booking.com】

Advertising

【51†5. EB Hotel Miami Airport】

  * Hotels 
  * Miami Springs

【51†Photograph: Courtesy Booking.com】

With luxe wooden furniture, warm orange accents and smooth marble features, this boutique hotel brings a hint of luxury to the area near Miami International Airport. The EB Hotel boasts an impressive location and a similarly impressive range of amenities making it one of the best places to stay in Miami for 21st-century travelers.

Where is it? Just 2.5 miles from the Miami International Airport and four miles from the waterfalls and grottoes of the Venetian Pool.

Which room? Travelling for work? The business suite has a small meeting room and lots of fancy tech gadgets and desk space to make it working away from the office easy. 

Time Out tip: Guests wanting some time to commune with nature might want to check out Amelia Earhart Park. Though it’s a solid 20-minute drive from the hotel, the park offers something for everyone. Kiddos will find endless entertainment in the farm village, petting zoo, skate park and playground, while grown-up adventure seekers can rent mountain bikes to traverse the park’s well-maintained trails.

【52†Check prices†www.booking.com】

### 6. Wyndham Garden Miami International Airport

[Image 2: Wyndham Garden Miami International Airport]

[Image 3: Wyndham Garden Miami International Airport]

booking.com 

Full of blue walls, carpets and furnishings, this slick hotel mirrors its surroundings with breezy aquamarine accents that remind you that despite being just a stone’s throw from the Miami airport runway, you’re also surrounded by the lagoons of Miami Springs. As well as an on-site diner serving US classics, a gym and a heated outdoor pool, the rooms here come with flat-screen TVs, coffee makers and seating areas. 

Where is it? A free shuttle service takes guests to and from Miami International Airport and Port Miami and the bustling Downtown area are within easy access. 

Which room? Opt for a King room if you’re after extra space. 

Time Out tip: As well as a shuttle service to the airport, the hotel also provides a shuttle to Port Miami’s cruise terminal for sightseeing on the water. 

【53†Check prices†www.booking.com】

Advertising

### 7. AC Hotel by Marriott

[Image 4: AC Hotel by Marriott]

[Image 5: AC Hotel by Marriott]

booking.com 

With a chic monochrome colour palette and unique European influences, AC Hotel by Marriott feels a cut above the traditional airport hotel. The rooms are sleek and minimal with dark wood floors, minimal desks and open closets. The public spaces like the AC lounge are filled with interesting art pieces and elegant bars. Reflecting Miami’s Spanish connections, the food here has plenty of Mediterranean inflexions, like the breakfast which offers sweet and savoury Spanish egg tarts and freshly sliced Iberico ham. While a tapas menu is on offer in the evenings. 

Where is it? Just 4 miles away from the airport and with easy access to downtown Doral and CityPlace Doral. 

Which room? The European rooms and slick, stylish and modern. 

Time Out tip: Don’t forget to hit up the outdoor pool and ask the bartenders for tips on what to do in the local area. 

【54

Updated for March 2024: We want you to end up at the very best hotel for you, which is why we've added even more choices to our list of hotels near Miami Airport. These include a convenience and comfort-forward property, and one with a secret sun terrace and outdoor pool.  

Who makes the cut? While we might not stay in and review every hotel featured, we've based our list on our expert knowledge of the destination covered, editorial reviews, user reviews, hotel amenities and in-depth research to find you the best stays. This article includes affiliate links. These links have no influence on our editorial content. For more information, see our 【42†affiliate】 【42†guidelines】.

Been there, done that? Think again, my friend.

Get into a relationship with our newsletter. Discover the best of the city, first.

Enter email address 

Déjà vu! We already have this email. Try another?

By entering your email address you agree to our 【0†Terms of Use】 and 【1†Privacy Policy】 and consent to receive emails from Time Out about news, events, offers and partner promotions.

Awesome, you're subscribed!

Thanks for subscribing! Look out for your first newsletter in your inbox soon!

## Best Miami airport hotels

【43†1. Hilton Miami Airport Blue Lagoon】

  * Hotels 
  * Allapattah

【43†Photograph: Courtesy Booking.com】

Airport hotels don't have to mean being surrounded by concrete. The Hilton Hotel is sat in the middle of a beautiful lagoon, that looks like a set from a Hollywood movie. The sleek spot caters to business travelers and vacationers alike with its spectacular vista, outdoor activities and functional workspaces.

Where is it? Four miles from the airport in leafy Blue Lagoon. Downtown Miami and Dolphin Mall are 15 minutes away.

Which room? Opt for a junior suite for extra space and stunning views. 

Time Out tip: Whether you’re used to sinking holes-in-one or have never picked up a putter before, you can surely wedge in nine holes at the Granada Golf Course. Opened in 1923, this historic course is among the oldest in the state. It’s also one of the best for beginners, with a fully stocked pro shop and no water hazards.  

【44†Check prices†www.booking.com】

【45†2. Pullman Miami Airport】

  * Hotels 
  * Blue Lagoon

【45†Photograph: Courtesy Booking.com】

Proof that the best Miami airport hotels offer more than just a decent night’s sleep, this convenient airport-adjacent hotel has much more flair than the standard options. In fact, to simply call the venue aesthetically pleasing would be an understatement, thanks to an interior laden with contemporary art and sophisticated furnishings and an exterior that evokes a sense of tropical grandeur.

Where is it? Just over 3 miles from the airport with a free shuttle service and minutes from Brickell City Centre, Downtown Miami, Port of Miami and beaches. 

Which room? Pick a lagoon side room for the best scenes from the window. 

Time Out tip: Traveling with family? The Pullman Miami Airport offers free accommodations and breakfast for up to two children under 12, so you can afford to bring the kids along on your next vacation. (We'll let you decide if that's good news or not).

【46†Check prices†www.booking.com】

Advertising

【47†3. Hyatt Regency Coral Gables in Miami】

  * Hotels 
  * Coral Gables

【47†Photograph: Courtesy Booking.com】

Old-world Spanish decor meets modern amenities in this charming Coral Gables hotel. At an easy distance from the strip, this airport hotel is not only good for those waiting for flights, but for those with an insatiable streak of Miami wanderlust, too.

Where is it? Six miles from downtown Miami in the heart of the fun-packed town of Coral Gables. 

Which room? We think the rooms with pool views really put the cherry on top if your stay. 

Time Out tip: No shade to the pool at the Hyatt Regency, but it just can’t compare to the crystal clear waters of the nearby Venetian Pool. The most gorgeous swimming hole in Coral Gables (if not the world) was once a coral rock quarry before it was turned into a full-service pool in the 1920s. Fed by a subterranean aquifer and flanked by palm trees, the freshwater pool looks impossibly idyllic. Since tourists descend on the pool over the weekend, you’ll want to visit on a weekday for a more serene swimming experience.

【48†Check prices†www.booking.com】

【49†4. Sheraton Miami Airport Hotel】

  * Hotels 
  * Miami

【49†Photograph: Courtesy Booking.com】

Don't let the humdrum exterior fool you, inside the Sheraton there’s some understated but impeccably stylish decor. But mostly, it's the proximity to an 18-hole golf course and an abundance of meeting rooms that make the Sheraton the perfect spot for business travelers.

Where is it? Little Havana and Marlins Park are on the doorstep. There’s also a free shuttle service runnig every 15 minutes 24-hours a day from the airport. 

Which room? The Traditional Rooms are easy on the wallet and offer great views and plenty of stylish amenities.  

Time Out tip: You can’t visit Little Havana without making a pilgrimage to Versailles, one of the city’s most iconic restaurants and a landmark in its own right. Ropa vieja, cubanos, seafood paella, flan: Versailles does all of it impeccably. Settle into a booth in the mirrored dining room, order up a Cuban feast and take in the ambiance—you won’t find anything like it anywhere else.

【50†Check prices†www.booking.com】

Advertising

【51†5. EB Hotel Miami Airport】

  * Hotels 
  * Miami Springs

【51†Photograph: Courtesy Booking.com】

With luxe wooden furniture, warm orange accents and smooth marble features, this boutique hotel brings a hint of luxury to the area near Miami International Airport. The EB Hotel boasts an impressive location and a similarly impressive range of amenities making it one of the best places to stay in Miami for 21st-century travelers.

Where is it? Just 2.5 miles from the Miami International Airport and four miles from the waterfalls and grottoes of the Venetian Pool.

Which room? Travelling for work? The business suite has a small meeting room and lots of fancy tech gadgets and desk space to make it working away from the office easy. 

Time Out tip: Guests wanting some time to commune with nature might want to check out Amelia Earhart Park. Though it’s a solid 20-minute drive from the hotel, the park offers something for everyone. Kiddos will find endless entertainment in the farm village, petting zoo, skate park and playground, while grown-up adventure seekers can rent mountain bikes to traverse the park’s well-maintained trails.

【52†Check prices†www.booking.com】

### 6. Wyndham Garden Miami International Airport

[Image 2: Wyndham Garden Miami International Airport]

[Image 3: Wyndham Garden Miami International Airport]

booking.com 

Full of blue walls, carpets and furnishings, this slick hotel mirrors its surroundings with breezy aquamarine accents that remind you that despite being just a stone’s throw from the Miami airport runway, you’re also surrounded by the lagoons of Miami Springs. As well as an on-site diner serving US classics, a gym and a heated outdoor pool, the rooms here come with flat-screen TVs, coffee makers and seating areas. 

Where is it? A free shuttle service takes guests to and from Miami International Airport and Port Miami and the bustling Downtown area are within easy access. 

Which room? Opt for a King room if you’re after extra space. 

Time Out tip: As well as a shuttle service to the airport, the hotel also provides a shuttle to Port Miami’s cruise terminal for sightseeing on the water. 

【53†Check prices†www.booking.com】

Advertising

### 7. AC Hotel by Marriott

[Image 4: AC Hotel by Marriott]

[Image 5: AC Hotel by Marriott]

booking.com 

With a chic monochrome colour palette and unique European influences, AC Hotel by Marriott feels a cut above the traditional airport hotel. The rooms are sleek and minimal with dark wood floors, minimal desks and open closets. The public spaces like the AC lounge are filled with interesting art pieces and elegant bars. Reflecting Miami’s Spanish connections, the food here has plenty of Mediterranean inflexions, like the breakfast which offers sweet and savoury Spanish egg tarts and freshly sliced Iberico ham. While a tapas menu is on offer in the evenings. 

Where is it? Just 4 miles away from the airport and with easy access to downtown Doral and CityPlace Doral. 

Which room? The European rooms and slick, stylish and modern. 

Time Out tip: Don’t forget to hit up the outdoor pool and ask the bartenders for tips on what to do in the local area. 

【54

The differences between Economy and Business Class seats on an Airbus A320 operated by American Airlines typically include the following:

### **Seating and Comfort:**
- **Business Class:** 
  - Larger, more spacious seats with extra legroom and width (typically around 37-39 inches of pitch and 20-22 inches wide).
  - Recline is significantly greater, offering more comfort, especially on longer flights.
  - Adjustable headrests and footrests are usually available.
  
- **Economy Class:**
  - Seats are smaller with less legroom and width (around 30-32 inches of pitch and 17-18 inches wide).
  - Limited recline and less overall cushioning.
  
### **In-Flight Service:**
- **Business Class:**
  - Complimentary meals and beverages, including alcohol on most flights.
  - Higher quality meals, often with more variety and served on proper dishes.
  - Dedicated flight attendants providing more attentive service.

- **Economy Class:**
  - Complimentary snacks and non-alcoholic beverages on shorter flights; meals may be available for purchase on longer flights.
  - Alcoholic beverages are available for purchase.
  
### **Entertainment:**
- **Business Class:**
  - Larger personal entertainment screens with noise-canceling headphones (if available).
  - More extensive selection of movies, TV shows, music, and games.
  
- **Economy Class:**
  - Smaller screens or shared overhead screens (depending on the aircraft version).
  - Basic entertainment selection, and in some cases, access to streaming via your device.

### **Amenities and Perks:**
- **Business Class:**
  - Priority check-in, security, boarding, and baggage handling.
  - Access to airport lounges where available.
  - Additional baggage allowance (typically two checked bags for free).

- **Economy Class:**
  - Standard boarding process.
  - Baggage fees may apply unless you have elite status or specific fare benefits.
  
### **Price:**
- Business Class tickets are substantially more expensive than Economy due to the added space, comfort, and amenities.

These differences make Business Class a more comfortable and luxurious option, especially for longer flights, while Economy Class provides a more cost-effective travel option.

No, Business Class is not exactly the same as what used to be called First Class, though the distinction can vary by airline and route:

### **Key Differences:**

1. **Terminology Evolution:**
   - **Domestic Flights:** On many U.S. domestic flights, what used to be called "First Class" is now often referred to as "Business Class" or still called "First Class." This can cause confusion, but they’re generally more similar to Business Class standards found on international flights rather than the traditional, more luxurious First Class experience.
   - **International Flights:** Traditionally, First Class was a step above Business Class, offering even more luxury, space, and exclusive amenities. However, many airlines have eliminated First Class on international flights in favor of an enhanced Business Class experience that merges some of the luxury elements of First Class.

2. **Seat and Cabin Differences:**
   - **Business Class:** Offers lie-flat seats on long-haul flights, spacious seating, high-quality meals, and enhanced service. However, Business Class typically doesn't match the extremely high level of privacy and luxury (such as fully enclosed suites) that First Class used to provide.
   - **First Class:** If available, First Class offers even more space, privacy (sometimes with enclosed suites), and additional luxury touches such as gourmet dining, premium champagne, and exclusive access to showers or private cabins (on select airlines like Emirates and Etihad).

3. **Service and Amenities:**
   - **Business Class:** Has elevated service, including priority boarding, higher-quality meals, and better baggage allowances compared to Economy.
   - **First Class:** Offers the most premium level of service, including the most attentive cabin crew-to-passenger ratio, exclusive amenities, top-notch dining, and access to the most luxurious airport lounges.

### **Current Trends:**
Many airlines have chosen to focus on improving Business Class and phasing out First Class, so the line between the two has blurred. Today, Business Class is often the top-tier product on many airlines, especially on domestic and shorter international flights. 

If you’re traveling on an Airbus A320 with American Airlines, their premium cabin is marketed as “First Class” for domestic routes but is comparable to what many airlines would consider Business Class in terms of comfort and amenities.

The main safety considerations for driving from the US to Panama City, Panama, include:

### 1. **Border Crossings and Paperwork**
   - **Documents:** Ensure you have all necessary travel documents, including a valid passport, driver’s license, vehicle registration, proof of insurance, and a Temporary Vehicle Import Permit (TVIP) for each country.
   - **Border Delays:** Border crossings can be time-consuming, taking anywhere from 1 to 6 hours. Be patient and vigilant with your documents.

### 2. **Crime and Security**
   - **Crime Risk:** Petty theft, robbery, and vehicle break-ins are common, especially near borders, in urban areas, and in remote regions. Avoid displaying valuables, and always lock your vehicle.
   - **Corruption:** Expect occasional encounters with corrupt officials seeking bribes. Stay calm, polite, and carry photocopies of your documents to minimize risk.

### 3. **Road Conditions and Driving Hazards**
   - **Road Quality:** Road conditions can vary widely. While highways are generally in good condition, some rural or mountainous roads can be poorly maintained, unpaved, or subject to landslides.
   - **Night Driving:** Avoid driving at night due to poor lighting, road hazards, stray animals, or unmarked construction.
   - **Traffic Rules:** Each country may have different driving rules and enforcement levels. Be cautious and adhere to local regulations.

### 4. **Health and Safety**
   - **Medical Emergencies:** Carry a basic first-aid kit and medications, as healthcare facilities may be limited or far apart, especially in remote areas.
   - **Water and Food Safety:** Always drink bottled or purified water and be cautious about where you eat to avoid foodborne illnesses.

### 5. **Natural Hazards**
   - **Weather:** Central America can have extreme weather, such as heavy rains or hurricanes, especially during the rainy season (May to November). Check weather forecasts regularly.
   - **Flooding and Landslides:** Roads can be prone to flooding or landslides during heavy rains, particularly in mountainous regions.

### 6. **Communication and Navigation**
   - **Cell Coverage:** Cell phone coverage may be limited in remote areas. Consider carrying a satellite phone or using apps with offline maps.
   - **Language Barrier:** Spanish is the primary language in all countries you'll pass through. Basic knowledge of Spanish will be very helpful.

### 7. **Vehicle Preparedness**
   - **Vehicle Maintenance:** Ensure your vehicle is in excellent condition, carry spare tires, extra fuel, and basic tools.
   - **Fuel Availability:** Gas stations can be scarce in remote areas, so keep your tank full whenever possible.

### Tips for Enhancing Safety:
- **Travel in Daylight:** Plan your travel during daylight hours to avoid risks associated with night driving.
- **Stay Informed:** Regularly check travel advisories for each country from sources like the U.S. State Department.
- **Travel with a Companion:** If possible, travel with a companion for added security.

4. **Safety:** Some areas along the route can be challenging or unsafe, so it's crucial to research each country’s travel advisories and plan accordingly.

The blue 4-pin plug on your 1997 150hp Yamaha outboard 2-stroke motor is typically used for diagnostic purposes and connects to the Yamaha diagnostic system or interface cable. This connector allows a technician to access the engine's data, including error codes, performance metrics, and other operational details.

If you're looking to connect it, you'd generally need a compatible Yamaha diagnostic tool or gauge that interfaces with this connector, often found in the helm area or used in a marine mechanic's setup. If you are planning to connect it to a gauge, NMEA 2000 network, or other monitoring system, you may require a Yamaha-specific adapter or signal converter to properly interface it.

Yes, the negative ground connection can often be located on or near the starter motor, as it's typically a convenient and effective grounding point on many outboard engines, including your 1997 150hp Yamaha 2-stroke.

However, in most cases, the negative battery cable will not connect directly to the starter motor itself but rather to a grounding bolt or stud on the engine block very close to the starter motor. This grounding point ensures a solid connection to the engine block, which in turn provides a reliable path for the starter and all other electrical systems.

Here's what you should do:

1. **Locate the Starter Motor:** Find the starter motor on your engine.
   
2. **Look for a Nearby Grounding Bolt or Stud:** Check around the starter motor for a bolt or stud where other grounding wires may already be connected or where it’s designed to connect the main ground cable.

3. **Attach the Negative Cable:** If you find this grounding point, ensure the connection is clean, free of corrosion, and tightly secured.

If the negative cable isn't reaching this area or you’re unsure, you may want to refer to the engine's service manual for the exact grounding location specific to your model. This will ensure you're connecting it to the optimal point for proper engine operation.

If your Yamaha outboard engine has power from the battery up to the point where it connects to the engine but no further, here’s a step-by-step troubleshooting guide:

1. **Check the Battery Connections:**
   - Ensure that the battery terminals are clean, tight, and free from corrosion.
   - Verify that the battery cables (both positive and negative) are in good condition, with no fraying or damage.

2. **Inspect the Main Fuse:**
   - Locate the main fuse near the engine’s wiring harness or where the battery cable connects to the engine. This is often a 20-30 amp fuse in a fuse holder.
   - Check if the fuse is blown or corroded. Replace it if necessary.

3. **Examine the Battery Cables and Connections:**
   - Inspect the positive and negative cables from the battery to the engine for any signs of damage or corrosion.
   - Make sure all connections are tight and secure at both ends.

4. **Check the Engine Ground:**
   - Ensure that the engine has a good ground connection. The negative battery cable should be securely connected to the engine block. 
   - Clean the grounding point to ensure a good electrical connection if you notice any rust or corrosion.

5. **Inspect the Engine's Key Switch:**
   - The ignition switch could be faulty or have loose connections. Check the wiring at the back of the ignition switch and ensure it’s properly connected.
   - Test the switch by using a multimeter to verify if it’s delivering power when turned to the "ON" position.

6. **Examine the Starter Solenoid:**
   - Check if the solenoid is receiving power from the battery. Use a multimeter to test for voltage at the solenoid's input terminal.
   - If the solenoid isn’t receiving power or isn’t functioning correctly, this could be the issue.

7. **Check Wiring Harness Connections:**
   - Look for any loose, damaged, or corroded connectors in the wiring harness between the battery, engine, and control box.
   - Re-seat the connectors by unplugging and plugging them back in to ensure a good connection.

8. **Test with a Multimeter:**
   - Use a multimeter to trace the power from the battery connection point to the engine components, such as the fuse, solenoid, ignition switch, and starter motor. This will help identify where the power loss occurs.

By following these steps, you should be able to identify where the power is lost beyond the connection point. If you're unable to locate the issue, it might be worth consulting a marine technician for further assistance.

Black oil coming out of the propeller exhaust when you start your 1997 150hp Yamaha outboard 2-stroke engine could indicate one of the following issues:

1. **Unburned Fuel and Oil Mixture:** In 2-stroke engines, a mix of fuel and oil lubricates the engine. If the engine has been idling for a long time, or if you’ve recently started it after sitting unused, some unburned oil and fuel can accumulate in the exhaust and then drain out when you start the engine. This is often normal for 2-stroke engines, especially if the engine is running rich or if you've been running at low speeds for an extended period.

2. **Excessive Fuel/Oil Ratio:** If your fuel mixture has too much oil, it can lead to excess unburned oil being expelled through the exhaust. Check that you’re using the correct oil-to-fuel ratio, which is typically around 50:1 for most Yamaha 2-stroke engines.

3. **Over-priming or Carburetor Issues:** If you’ve over-primed the engine or if the carburetors are flooding, excess fuel and oil can pass through the combustion chamber unburned and exit through the exhaust.

4. **Oil Leakage from the Lower Unit:** Sometimes, oil from the gearcase or lower unit can mix with the exhaust. This might indicate a seal or gasket issue in the lower unit, allowing gear oil to escape and mix with the exhaust. If the oil has a strong, burnt smell or feels thicker, this could be gear oil.

5. **Residual Carbon and Oil Build-up:** Over time, carbon, unburned oil, and fuel can build up in the exhaust system. When the engine starts, these residues can be expelled through the propeller exhaust.

**What to Do Next:**

- **Check the Oil/Fuel Ratio:** Make sure you're using the correct oil-to-fuel mix. 
- **Inspect the Oil:** Check the oil's consistency and smell. Gear oil has a strong sulfur smell, while fuel/oil mixture will smell like gasoline.
- **Examine the Spark Plugs:** Remove and inspect the spark plugs. If they’re fouled with oil or carbon, it might indicate a fuel mixture issue or that the engine isn't burning fuel efficiently.
- **Monitor Performance:** Run the engine and monitor how it behaves. If it’s running rough, smoking excessively, or not reaching full RPMs, there may be a carburetor, fuel, or internal engine issue.
- **Check for Gear Oil Leak:** Inspect the lower unit for any signs of oil leakage, such as oil stains or droplets around the seals or water intakes.

If the problem persists or you suspect a gear oil leak, it’s advisable to have a marine technician inspect the engine to prevent further damage.

If your engine ran well previously but has been sitting unused for a month, it's possible that the following issues have developed during that time:

1. **Stale Fuel:** Fuel left in the carburetor, fuel lines, or tank can deteriorate over time, especially in a month. Ethanol-blended fuels are particularly prone to absorbing moisture, leading to phase separation, which can cause starting issues. Old fuel can prevent proper combustion, leading to unburned fuel exiting through the exhaust.

   **Solution:** Drain the old fuel from the tank and replace it with fresh fuel. If possible, add a fuel stabilizer to help prevent this issue in the future.

2. **Carburetor Gumming:** Fuel can evaporate and leave behind a sticky residue in the carburetor, leading to clogged jets or sticky floats. This can result in a rich mixture or flooding, preventing the engine from running properly.

   **Solution:** Clean the carburetors, ensuring all jets, passages, and floats are free of any residue or blockages.

3. **Moisture or Condensation:** Moisture can build up in the fuel tank, carburetor, or ignition components when an engine sits unused, especially in humid environments. This can cause poor fuel quality or interfere with ignition.

   **Solution:** Check the fuel tank for water contamination, and inspect ignition components for moisture or corrosion. Using a fuel/water separator is a good preventative measure for future use.

4. **Spark Plug Fouling:** If the engine sat without being run, oil may have accumulated on the spark plugs, or they may have developed carbon deposits. This can prevent proper ignition.

   **Solution:** Remove, inspect, clean, or replace the spark plugs as needed.

5. **Battery and Electrical Connections:** Corrosion can build up on battery terminals, grounding points, or electrical connections over time, leading to weak or inconsistent power to the ignition system.

   **Solution:** Clean all battery terminals, ground connections, and other wiring connections to ensure good conductivity.

**Recommended First Steps:**

- Drain and replace the fuel with fresh gasoline.
- Inspect and clean the carburetor if you suspect gumming.
- Check and clean or replace the spark plugs.
- Inspect the battery connections and ensure the electrical system is functioning correctly.

These steps should help in getting your engine back to running condition. If it still doesn’t start after addressing these areas, you might need to dig deeper into potential carburetor or fuel pump issues.

The negative (ground) cable from the battery should be securely connected to a designated grounding point on the engine block. For your 1997 150hp Yamaha outboard 2-stroke motor, the typical grounding location is usually:

1. **Engine Block Grounding Bolt:** There should be a specific bolt or stud on the engine block designed for grounding purposes. It's often located near the starter motor or on one of the larger metal surfaces of the engine block. This connection provides the main ground path for all electrical components.

2. **Clean the Grounding Point:** Ensure that the grounding bolt or stud is free from corrosion, paint, or any debris, as these can prevent a good electrical connection. You may need to clean it with a wire brush to expose clean, bare metal.

3. **Tighten the Connection:** The ground cable should be tightly secured to the grounding point using a nut. Make sure the cable's eyelet connector is clean and making good contact with the block.

Always double-check that this connection is solid, as a poor ground can cause a range of electrical problems, including issues with starting, charging, or running the engine.

No, a corroded yellow wire with a white stripe (the RPM/tachometer signal wire) typically would **not** prevent the engine from starting. This wire is primarily used to send RPM data to the tachometer gauge and isn't part of the engine's starting or ignition circuits.

However, if your engine isn't starting, there could be other reasons, such as:

1. **Battery Issues:** Check if the battery is fully charged and has good connections.
2. **Main Electrical Connections:** Ensure all battery cables (positive and negative) and engine ground connections are secure and corrosion-free.
3. **Fuses:** Inspect all fuses to ensure none are blown.
4. **Ignition Switch:** Verify the ignition switch is functioning correctly.
5. **Starter Solenoid/Relay:** Check if the solenoid clicks when you turn the key, indicating it’s working.
6. **Kill Switch or Safety Lanyard:** Make sure the kill switch is in the "run" position, as it will prevent the engine from starting if activated.

The tachometer wire being corroded could indicate more widespread corrosion, which could potentially affect other wires that are essential for starting the engine. So while that specific wire isn't the cause, it's worth inspecting and cleaning all connections to ensure there’s no other corrosion impacting the starting circuit.

If the black oil smells like fuel and the engine won't run, it indicates that unburned fuel is likely accumulating in the exhaust system, which suggests one of the following issues:

1. **Flooding or Carburetor Issue:** The carburetors may be flooding, causing excess fuel to enter the combustion chambers without igniting properly. This can happen if the float is stuck, the needle valve isn’t sealing, or if there is debris in the carburetor. A flooded engine will usually have difficulty starting.

2. **Spark Plug Problem:** Worn-out, fouled, or wet spark plugs can prevent the engine from firing correctly. This would result in unburned fuel passing through the exhaust. Check and clean or replace the spark plugs if necessary.

3. **Fuel Pump Malfunction:** A faulty fuel pump could be delivering too much fuel or failing to regulate the fuel pressure properly, leading to excessive fuel entering the engine.

4. **Reed Valve Issue:** The reed valves control the flow of air and fuel mixture into the crankcase. If the reed valves are damaged or not sealing properly, this can lead to poor fuel atomization and unburned fuel entering the exhaust.

5. **Ignition System Fault:** If the ignition system is not delivering a consistent spark (e.g., a bad coil, CDI unit, or stator), the fuel mixture won't ignite correctly, causing unburned fuel to exit through the exhaust.

**Recommended Actions:**

- **Check the Spark Plugs:** Remove and inspect them to see if they're wet, fouled, or damaged. Clean or replace them as needed.
- **Inspect the Carburetors:** If you're comfortable working on the engine, check for any debris, stuck floats, or needle valve issues. You may need to clean or rebuild the carburetors.
- **Examine the Fuel Pump:** Check for leaks or signs of damage. Replace it if it's not functioning correctly.
- **Test the Ignition System:** Verify that all cylinders are receiving a strong spark. You can use a spark tester to do this.

If you're unsure or unable to diagnose the problem, it’s best to consult a marine technician for a thorough inspection and repair.

Debt payments themselves are not directly deductible or included in the calculation of your Adjusted Gross Income (AGI). However, it depends on the context of the debt and the type of payment. Here’s how debt is generally treated in terms of AGI calculations:

### 1. **Personal Debt Payments (e.g., Personal Loans, Credit Cards)**
- **Principal Payments**: The repayment of the loan's principal (the original amount borrowed) is not deductible and does not affect your AGI. It’s simply paying back money you borrowed.
- **Interest Payments**: Interest on personal loans or credit card debt is also not deductible unless it qualifies under specific exceptions, such as student loan interest or mortgage interest.

### 2. **Mortgage Interest**
- **Mortgage Interest**: If you itemize your deductions, you can deduct mortgage interest payments on your primary or secondary residence. This deduction doesn’t directly reduce your AGI but lowers your taxable income after AGI is calculated.

### 3. **Business Debt Payments**
- If the debt is related to a **business expense**, the treatment is different:
  - **Interest Payments**: The interest paid on business loans is deductible as a business expense on your Schedule C (for sole proprietors) or other relevant tax forms, which reduces your net business income and thus your AGI.
  - **Principal Payments**: Repaying the principal of a business loan is not deductible and does not directly impact AGI.

### 4. **Capital Gains or Losses and Debt Payments**
- In the case of selling a property or asset, if you used debt to finance the purchase or improvements, the debt itself doesn’t affect your AGI. Instead, it’s the **cost basis** (purchase price plus improvements and expenses) that determines your gain or loss, which then affects your AGI.
- For example, if you paid off debt with proceeds from a property sale, this payoff doesn't reduce your AGI. Instead, your AGI is affected by the gain or loss from the sale, calculated as the difference between the sale price and your adjusted cost basis.

### **Key Points:**
- **Personal debt payments** (principal and interest) are not deductible and do not reduce your AGI.
- **Business-related interest payments** are deductible as a business expense and reduce your AGI if they are related to generating business income.
- **Mortgage interest** is deductible if you itemize but doesn’t affect AGI directly—it reduces taxable income afterward.

For the tax year 2019, there are specific thresholds that determine whether you owe income tax or self-employment tax:

### 1. **Income Tax Threshold**
- The **standard deduction** for 2019 was:
  - **$12,200** for single filers
  - **$24,400** for married couples filing jointly
  - **$18,350** for heads of household

If your total income after deductions (adjusted gross income or AGI) is **less than the standard deduction**, you would not owe any federal income tax. 

For example:
- If your net profit was $15,000 and you were single, the standard deduction of $12,200 would reduce your taxable income to $2,800. However, if you had other deductions, credits, or a capital loss offset, your taxable income might be further reduced to zero, meaning no income tax would be due.

### 2. **Self-Employment Tax Threshold**
- Self-employment tax kicks in if your **net earnings from self-employment** are **$400 or more**. This means even if your overall income is below the income tax threshold, you are still required to pay self-employment tax on net earnings over $400.
- The self-employment tax rate is 15.3%, which consists of 12.4% for Social Security and 2.9% for Medicare.

### **Summary**
- If your net self-employment income is **less than $400**, you will not owe any self-employment tax.
- For federal income tax, if your income after deductions is **below the standard deduction** (e.g., $12,200 for a single filer), you won't owe any income tax.

So, there is no threshold below which you entirely avoid both taxes unless your self-employment income is under $400, or your overall income after deductions is below the standard deduction.

## Vintage-Inspired Cat-Eye Glasses

Capture a retro feminine look in your everyday wardrobe with a pair of cat-eye eyeglasses or sunglasses. Originally popularized in the mid-20th century, when eyewear became a 【152†fashion accessory】 rather than a medical necessity, cat-eye frames remain a favorite among glasses wearers. Cat-eye glasses impart sophisticated, elegant, outgoing style to the most casual outfit, and come in eyeglass, sunglass, and 【153†prescription sunglass options for women and girls】.

## Cat-Eye Glasses FAQs

What Makes a Pair of Sunglasses or Eyeglasses Cat-Eye?

The classic cat-eye silhouette is synonymous with the familiar butterfly shape and features rounded lenses and upswept corners that subtly mimic the eyes of a cat. These delineating features of the iconic style can be embellished with rhinestone, metal, or 【154†colored plastic enhancements】 as opulent extras, while sculptural effects—raised designs, prominent browlines, scalloped edges, and fancy bridges—offer unique accents.

Are Cat Eye Glasses in Style?

Cat-eye glasses have remained in style and on-trend for more than half a century. While upswept endpoints and an arching browline characterize the timeless look, cat-eye glasses come in a range of sizes, materials, and patterns to suit nearly any 【155†face shape】 and taste. Originally popularized in the mid-20th century, when eyewear became a 【152†fashion accessory】 rather than a medical necessity, cat-eye frames remain a favorite among glasses wearers. ## Cat-Eye Glasses FAQs

What Makes a Pair of Sunglasses or Eyeglasses Cat-Eye?

The classic cat-eye silhouette is synonymous with the familiar butterfly shape and features rounded lenses and upswept corners that subtly mimic the eyes of a cat. Cat-eye glasses have remained in style and on-trend for more than half a century. ## Vintage-Inspired Cat-Eye Glasses

Capture a retro feminine look in your everyday wardrobe with a pair of cat-eye eyeglasses or sunglasses. Originally popularized in the mid-20th century, when eyewear became a 【152†fashion accessory】 rather than a medical necessity, cat-eye frames remain a favorite among glasses wearers. Cat-eye glasses impart sophisticated, elegant, outgoing style to the most casual outfit, and come in eyeglass, sunglass, and 【153†prescription sunglass options for women and girls】.

## Cat-Eye Glasses FAQs

What Makes a Pair of Sunglasses or Eyeglasses Cat-Eye?

The classic cat-eye silhouette is synonymous with the familiar butterfly shape and features rounded lenses and upswept corners that subtly mimic the eyes of a cat. These delineating features of the iconic style can be embellished with rhinestone, metal, or 【154†colored plastic enhancements】 as opulent extras, while sculptural effects—raised designs, prominent browlines, scalloped edges, and fancy bridges—offer unique accents.

Are Cat Eye Glasses in Style?

Cat-eye glasses have remained in style and on-trend for more than half a century. While upswept endpoints and an arching browline characterize the timeless look, cat-eye glasses come in a range of sizes, materials, and patterns to suit nearly any 【155†face shape】 and taste. ### Frequently Asked Questions about Cat Eye Glasses 

What are the best face shapes for cat eye glasses?

Cat eye frames look great on individuals with heart-shaped, square, or oval face shapes. The upward angle of the frame can help draw attention upwards and balance broader jawlines.【29†Read our guide to choosing the right cat eye frame for your face shape.】

Are cat eye glasses in style for 2024?

Yes, cat eye glasses continue to be in style for 2024. This timeless design comes in a variety of patterns and colors, making them a staple in any wardrobe. They are a classic eyewear choice that combines vintage charm with a contemporary feel.【30† Read more about cat eye frames here.】

What face shapes are not the best fit for cat eye glasses?

Cat eye glasses suit most faces, but they tend to accentuate certain facial features. Generally, those with angular or square face shapes may find round or rimless frames to be a better balance. 【29† Read our guide to choosing the right cat eye frame for your face shape.】

Do cat eye glasses make you look younger?

Cat eye glasses can indeed make you look younger. Their distinctive upward tilt at the corners can lift the face visually, giving a more youthful appearance. The playful yet sophisticated shape of cat eye frames is a classic and timeless style statement. 【31†Learn how to style your eyewear for different occasions here.】

What glasses look best on an older face?

For an older face, glasses that lift and frame the face without overwhelming it are most suited. Lightweight frames in clear or neutral colors can be flattering, as well as softer rectangular or oval shapes.【32†Read our guide for choosing the right glasses for your age.】

## Vintage-Inspired Cat-Eye Glasses

Capture a retro feminine look in your everyday wardrobe with a pair of cat-eye eyeglasses or sunglasses. Originally popularized in the mid-20th century, when eyewear became a 【152†fashion accessory】 rather than a medical necessity, cat-eye frames remain a favorite among glasses wearers. Cat-eye glasses impart sophisticated, elegant, outgoing style to the most casual outfit, and come in eyeglass, sunglass, and 【153†prescription sunglass options for women and girls】.

## Cat-Eye Glasses FAQs

What Makes a Pair of Sunglasses or Eyeglasses Cat-Eye?

The classic cat-eye silhouette is synonymous with the familiar butterfly shape and features rounded lenses and upswept corners that subtly mimic the eyes of a cat. These delineating features of the iconic style can be embellished with rhinestone, metal, or 【154†colored plastic enhancements】 as opulent extras, while sculptural effects—raised designs, prominent browlines, scalloped edges, and fancy bridges—offer unique accents.

Are Cat Eye Glasses in Style?

Cat-eye glasses have remained in style and on-trend for more than half a century. While upswept endpoints and an arching browline characterize the timeless look, cat-eye glasses come in a range of sizes, materials, and patterns to suit nearly any 【155†face shape】 and taste. ### Frequently Asked Questions about Cat Eye Glasses 

What are the best face shapes for cat eye glasses?

Cat eye frames look great on individuals with heart-shaped, square, or oval face shapes. The upward angle of the frame can help draw attention upwards and balance broader jawlines.【29†Read our guide to choosing the right cat eye frame for your face shape.】

Are cat eye glasses in style for 2024?

Yes, cat eye glasses continue to be in style for 2024. This timeless design comes in a variety of patterns and colors, making them a staple in any wardrobe. They are a classic eyewear choice that combines vintage charm with a contemporary feel.【30† Read more about cat eye frames here.】

What face shapes are not the best fit for cat eye glasses?

Cat eye glasses suit most faces, but they tend to accentuate certain facial features. Generally, those with angular or square face shapes may find round or rimless frames to be a better balance. 【29† Read our guide to choosing the right cat eye frame for your face shape.】

Do cat eye glasses make you look younger?

Cat eye glasses can indeed make you look younger. Their distinctive upward tilt at the corners can lift the face visually, giving a more youthful appearance. The playful yet sophisticated shape of cat eye frames is a classic and timeless style statement. 【31†Learn how to style your eyewear for different occasions here.】

What glasses look best on an older face?

For an older face, glasses that lift and frame the face without overwhelming it are most suited. Lightweight frames in clear or neutral colors can be flattering, as well as softer rectangular or oval shapes.【32†Read our guide for choosing the right glasses for your age.】

As a traveler to Panama City, Panama, here are the top 3 cultural aspects to be aware of:

1. **Warm Greetings and Politeness**: Panamanians value polite greetings and courtesy. When meeting someone, it's customary to greet them with a handshake, and among friends, women may kiss each other on one cheek. Always greet people with "buenos días" (good morning), "buenas tardes" (good afternoon), or "buenas noches" (good evening). Being polite and showing respect is highly appreciated.

2. **Respect for Personal Space and Punctuality**: While Panamanians are warm and friendly, they respect personal space and prefer a bit of distance when conversing. Be mindful not to be overly touchy unless you have developed a closer relationship. Punctuality can be flexible in social settings, but it's still appreciated in professional or formal situations.

3. **Appreciation of Local Traditions and Heritage**: Panamanians take pride in their diverse heritage, including influences from Indigenous, Afro-Caribbean, Spanish, and American cultures. Showing interest and appreciation for their traditions, food, music, and history will be well-received. However, avoid political discussions or comments about sensitive issues like the Panama Canal unless you have a good understanding of the topic.

Here are two more unique aspects of Panamanian culture related to food, drink, and social etiquette, along with their phonetic pronunciations:

### **Food:**
1. **Carimañolas (Stuffed Yuca Fritters)** – These are fried yuca (cassava) fritters filled with ground meat or cheese. They are a popular breakfast or snack option, often served with a side of spicy sauce.
   - **Phonetic Pronunciation**: *Kah-ree-mah-nyo-lahs*

2. **Patacones (Fried Green Plantains)** – Slices of green plantains that are fried, flattened, and fried again until crispy. Patacones are a common side dish and are served with various meals.
   - **Phonetic Pronunciation**: *Pah-tah-coh-nes*

### **Drinks:**
1. **Chicheme –** A traditional non-alcoholic drink made from corn, milk, vanilla, cinnamon, and sugar. It's thick, sweet, and often served chilled, especially on hot days.
   - **Phonetic Pronunciation**: *Chee-cheh-meh*

2. **Balboa Beer –** One of Panama’s most popular local beers, named after the Spanish explorer Vasco Núñez de Balboa. It’s a light and refreshing lager that is widely enjoyed by locals and visitors alike.
   - **Phonetic Pronunciation**: *Bal-bo-ah beer*

### **Social Etiquette:**
1. **Punctuality in Social Settings –** While punctuality is expected for business meetings, it's common for social events to start 15-30 minutes later than the stated time. Panamanians have a more relaxed approach to time when it comes to social gatherings.
   - **Phonetic Pronunciation**: *Punk-tu-ah-lee-dad en so-see-al*

2. **Using Titles and Formal Address –** Panamanians place importance on addressing others with respect. Use formal titles such as “Señor” (Mr.), “Señora” (Mrs.), or “Señorita” (Miss) followed by the person's last name, especially in formal or business settings.
   - **Phonetic Pronunciation**: *Seh-nyor, Seh-nyo-rah, Seh-nyo-ree-tah*

These additional examples highlight the diverse and rich elements of Panamanian culture in food, drink, and social interactions. Would you like more insights into any of these aspects?

Here are some unique aspects of Panamanian culture related to food, drink, and social etiquette, along with their phonetic pronunciations:

### **Food:**
1. **Sancocho (Chicken Stew) –** This is Panama's national dish, a hearty chicken soup made with yucca, corn, and various vegetables. It's a popular comfort food enjoyed at family gatherings or celebrations.
   - **Phonetic Pronunciation**: *San-ko-cho*

2. **Ropa Vieja (Shredded Beef) –** A flavorful dish made from shredded beef cooked with onions, peppers, tomatoes, and spices, often served with rice. It's a staple in Panamanian cuisine and reflects the country's Spanish influence.
   - **Phonetic Pronunciation**: *Ro-pah vee-eh-hah*

### **Drinks:**
1. **Chicha de Saril (Hibiscus Tea) –** A popular holiday drink made from hibiscus flowers, cinnamon, ginger, and sugar. It's refreshing and served cold, especially around Christmas.
   - **Phonetic Pronunciation**: *Chee-cha deh sah-reel*

2. **Seco Herrerano –** A traditional Panamanian spirit made from sugarcane, similar to rum. It's often mixed with fruit juices or coconut water. Seco is the national liquor and is enjoyed in many social gatherings.
   - **Phonetic Pronunciation**: *Seh-ko heh-reh-rah-noh*

### **Social Etiquette:**
1. **Greeting with a Kiss on the Cheek –** When meeting someone, especially women, it's common to greet with a single kiss on the right cheek. Men usually shake hands but might also greet close female friends or family with a cheek kiss.
   - **Phonetic Pronunciation**: *Bee-so en la meh-hee-yah*

2. **Inviting Guests for Meals –** When invited to someone's home for a meal, it's polite to bring a small gift, like wine, flowers, or dessert. Panamanians value hospitality and enjoy sharing meals as a way of bonding.
   - **Phonetic Pronunciation**: *In-vee-tah-do pa-ra co-meer*

### Nuestra historia 

Nuestra historia comienza en Ciudad de Panamá, donde tres visionarios, la Dra. Maria Paula Serrano, el Dr. Guido Posada y Angelica Pínzon, fundaron Momentum Holding INC. Que se divide en Momentum Wellness Center, Momentum Wellness Academy y Momentum Wellness Distribution. Su pasión por la innovación y el deseo de brindar soluciones efectivas a los profesionales de la salud dental, impulsaron el crecimiento del negocio.

Soluciones duraderas y estéticas para reemplazar dientes perdidos.

Tratamiento de dientes con problemas de pulpa (tejido interior del diente) utilizando técnicas y herramientas microscópicas.

La estética dental abarca un amplio abanico de tratamientos, desde procedimientos simples como el blanqueamiento dental, hasta tratamientos más complejos como la colocación de implantes dentales o la ortodoncia. 

[Image 4]

Nos encargamos de prevenir, diagnosticar y tratar las enfermedades de las encías y los huesos que sostienen los dientes. Los servicios incluyen limpieza profesional, tratamiento de enfermedades periodontales, cirugía de encías y mantenimiento de la salud bucal para prevenir la pérdida de dientes.

[Image 6]

### Medicina estetica 

Nos enfocamos en mejorar la apariencia y la calidad de vida de las personas mediante tratamientos no invasivos o mínimamente invasivos. Los servicios incluyen rejuvenecimiento facial, rellenos dérmicos, tratamientos para arrugas, eliminación de manchas, tratamientos para celulitis y corporales, y mucho más. 

[Image 7]

Yes, T-Mobile provides international roaming services in Panama City, Panama. If you have a qualifying T-Mobile plan, you can enjoy free data and texting, along with low flat-rate calling in over 215 countries, including Panama. The specific T-Mobile plans that offer this coverage include Go5G, Magenta, ONE Plan, and Simple Choice plans, among others. If you're on an Essentials plan, you can get unlimited texting, but data usage will require an International Pass 【7†source】【8†source】【9†source】.

metadata.text:
How do I know which countries have free data and texting available? 

【8†Click here】 to see if you’re traveling to one of the 215+ countries that gets free data and texting as part of your eligible plan.

I’m going on a cruise. what do I need to know? 

You can check your cruise coverage 【9†here】. We recommend that you turn off roaming while the ship is docked in a US port. Otherwise, your phone may pick up the ship's network, and you'll be charged cruise ship roaming charges for any usage. Once you're out to sea, you can turn roaming back on and pay for the data, text, and voice you use.  

What is an international roaming plan? 

International roaming is a service allowing you to continue using your mobile phone or other mobile device to browse the internet, as well as send and receive: emails, voice calls, and text messages while visiting another country.

Will I get charged for using Wi-Fi internationally? 

The price you pay for Wi-Fi calls to international numbers when you're outside the US, depends on your international roaming option. The good news is, with most of our international roaming add-ons, you'll pay less for these calls than you did before. All Wi-Fi calls to US numbers are free of charge.

Is it free to text internationally with T-Mobile? 

Our most popular plans include international texting from home and while traveling. 【8†Click here】 to see if you’re traveling to one of the 215+ countries and destinations that gets data and texting as part of your eligible plan.

Will I incur charges if I receive a call while traveling internationally? 

Great news, while roaming internationally, you won't be charged for voicemails left in your inbox if your phone remains powered off or in airplane mode. However, you will be charged for the following:

  * If you answer an incoming call, you will be charged for the duration of the call.
  * If your phone is on when you get an incoming call, even if you don't answer it and it goes to voicemail, the call is charged one minute for the call coming into the phone, based on the 【10†international roaming rate 】 of the country you’re in. (There are no charges at all if your phone is turned off.)
  * If you call your voicemail from your mobile phone to listen to messages while traveling internationally, that call will be charged at the international roaming rate of the country you're in.  

Check out our 【11†international roaming checklist】 for everything you need to know before traveling abroad.

Which destinations do not include international roaming benefits? 

If you are a T-Mobile customer on qualifying plan, we have you covered with free data and texting in 215+ countries. There are some countries in which international roaming benefits do not apply, and international data passes cannot be used, you can check the list of those countries 【12†here】.

What should I know about using a VPN while traveling internationally? 

A Virtual Private Network (VPN), is a way to help keep your connection secure, even while traveling. Be aware, that while on Wi-fi and connected to a VPN, your Internet usage goes through the VPN network you are connected to, wherever it's located. This means that while connected to a U.S. based VPN network, Wi-Fi calls made to non-US numbers, while outside the U.S., will be charged at international long-distance rates. See more details 【13†here】.  

Heads up! Many VPN services may connect automatically, or even be included in other services such as AdBlockers.   

What T-Mobile plans qualify for international roaming benefits? 

  * Up to 5GB of high-speed data in 215+ countries and destinations: Go5G Next, Go5G Next Military, Go5G Next 55, Go5G Next First Responders, Go5G Next Puerto Rico, Go5G Next DHH, Go5G Business Next, Go5G Military Business Next, Go5G First Responder Business Next, Go5G Puerto Rico Business Next, Go5G DHH Business Next, Go5G Plus™, Go5G Plus Military, Go5G Plus 55+, Go5G Plus First Responder, Go5G Plus DHH, Go5G Business Plus, Go5G Military Business Plus, Go5G First Responder Business Plus, Business Unlimited Ultimate+, Go5G Puerto Rico Business Plus, Go5G DHH Business Plus, Magenta® MAX (including 55+, Military, and First Responder), Magenta® Plus, Magenta® MAX for Business, ONE Plus, Business Unlimited Ultimate, and Magenta® Amplified.
  * Up to 5GB of high-speed data in 11 European countries: Go5G™, Go5G Military, Go5G 55+, Go5G First Responder, Go5G DHH, Go5G Business, Go5G Military Business, Go5G First Responder Business, Go5G Puerto Rico Business, Go5G DHH Business, Magenta® (including 55+, Military, and First Responder), Magenta® Deaf or Hard of Hearing, Business Unlimited Select, Business Unlimited Advanced, and Magenta® for Business. Simple Choice, Select Choice, and ONE plans are also included.
  * Unlimited data speeds up to 256kbps: Go5G™, Go5G Military, Go5G 55+, Go5G First Responder, Go5G DHH, Go5G Business, Go5G Military Business, Go5G First Responder Business, Go5G Puerto Rico Business, Go5G DHH Business, Go5G Plus™, Go5G Plus Military, Go5G Plus 55+, Go5G Plus First Responder, Go5G Plus DHH, Go5G Business Plus, Go5G Military Business Plus, Go5G First Responder Business Plus, Business Unlimited Ultimate+, Go5G Puerto Rico Business Plus, Go5G DHH Business Plus, Magenta®, Magenta® MAX, Magenta 55+, Magenta® MAX 55+, Magenta® First Responder, Magenta® MAX First Responder, Magenta® Military, Magenta® MAX Military, Magenta® Deaf or Hard of Hearing, Magenta® MAX Deaf or Hard of Hearing, Magenta® Amplified, Business Unlimited Select, Business Unlimited Advanced, Business Unlimited Ultimate, Magenta® for Business, and Magenta® MAX for Business rate plans. Simple Choice, Select Choice, and ONE plans are also included.

Everyone on a T-Mobile Essentials™ plan gets unlimited texting and calling at $0.25 per minute in 215+ countries and destinations.

I have an Essentials™ plan. Do I get international roaming benefits? 

Essentials™ plans get free texting in 215+ countries and destinations. If you need data, purchase International Passes to get high-speed data and unlimited calling for 1, 10, or 30 days.

How can I get additional data and unlimited calling when traveling abroad? 

If you’re a T-Mobile customer on qualifying plan, you can add an International Pass to get more high-speed data and unlimited voice calling in 215+ countries and destinations.  

  * 1-Day (512MB) International Pass: 512MB of high-speed data and unlimited calling, to be used up to 24 hours, for $5.
  * 10 day (5GB) International Pass: 5GB of high-speed data and unlimited calling, to be used up to 10 days, for $35.
  * 30 Day (15GB) International Pass: 15GB of high-speed data and unlimited calling, to be used up to 30 days, for $50.

Use your International Pass high-speed data however you’d like throughout the designated time. You’re not restricted to a certain amount of data per day.

Great news, while roaming internationally, you won't be charged for voicemails left in your inbox if your phone remains powered off or in airplane mode. However, you will be charged for the following:

  * If you answer an incoming call, you will be charged for the duration of the call.

How do I know which countries have free data and texting available? 

【8†Click here】 to see if you’re traveling to one of the 215+ countries that gets free data and texting as part of your eligible plan.

I’m going on a cruise. what do I need to know? 

You can check your cruise coverage 【9†here】. We recommend that you turn off roaming while the ship is docked in a US port. Otherwise, your phone may pick up the ship's network, and you'll be charged cruise ship roaming charges for any usage. Once you're out to sea, you can turn roaming back on and pay for the data, text, and voice you use.  

What is an international roaming plan? 

International roaming is a service allowing you to continue using your mobile phone or other mobile device to browse the internet, as well as send and receive: emails, voice calls, and text messages while visiting another country.

Will I get charged for using Wi-Fi internationally? 

The price you pay for Wi-Fi calls to international numbers when you're outside the US, depends on your international roaming option. The good news is, with most of our international roaming add-ons, you'll pay less for these calls than you did before. All Wi-Fi calls to US numbers are free of charge.

Is it free to text internationally with T-Mobile? 

Our most popular plans include international texting from home and while traveling. 【8†Click here】 to see if you’re traveling to one of the 215+ countries and destinations that gets data and texting as part of your eligible plan.

Will I incur charges if I receive a call while traveling internationally? 

Great news, while roaming internationally, you won't be charged for voicemails left in your inbox if your phone remains powered off or in airplane mode. However, you will be charged for the following:

  * If you answer an incoming call, you will be charged for the duration of the call.
  * If your phone is on when you get an incoming call, even if you don't answer it and it goes to voicemail, the call is charged one minute for the call coming into the phone, based on the 【10†international roaming rate 】 of the country you’re in. (There are no charges at all if your phone is turned off.)
  * If you call your voicemail from your mobile phone to listen to messages while traveling internationally, that call will be charged at the international roaming rate of the country you're in.  

Check out our 【11†international roaming checklist】 for everything you need to know before traveling abroad.

Which destinations do not include international roaming benefits? 

If you are a T-Mobile customer on qualifying plan, we have you covered with free data and texting in 215+ countries. There are some countries in which international roaming benefits do not apply, and international data passes cannot be used, you can check the list of those countries 【12†here】.

What should I know about using a VPN while traveling internationally? 

A Virtual Private Network (VPN), is a way to help keep your connection secure, even while traveling. Be aware, that while on Wi-fi and connected to a VPN, your Internet usage goes through the VPN network you are connected to, wherever it's located. This means that while connected to a U.S. based VPN network, Wi-Fi calls made to non-US numbers, while outside the U.S., will be charged at international long-distance rates. See more details 【13†here】.  

Heads up! Many VPN services may connect automatically, or even be included in other services such as AdBlockers.

  * Up to 5GB of high-speed data in 11 European countries: Go5G™, Go5G Military, Go5G 55+, Go5G First Responder, Go5G DHH, Go5G Business, Go5G Military Business, Go5G First Responder Business, Go5G Puerto Rico Business, Go5G DHH Business, Magenta® (including 55+, Military, and First Responder), Magenta® Deaf or Hard of Hearing, Business Unlimited Select, Business Unlimited Advanced, and Magenta® for Business. Simple Choice, Select Choice, and ONE plans are also included.
  * Unlimited data speeds up to 256kbps: Go5G™, Go5G Military, Go5G 55+, Go5G First Responder, Go5G DHH, Go5G Business, Go5G Military Business, Go5G First Responder Business, Go5G Puerto Rico Business, Go5G DHH Business, Go5G Plus™, Go5G Plus Military, Go5G Plus 55+, Go5G Plus First Responder, Go5G Plus DHH, Go5G Business Plus, Go5G Military Business Plus, Go5G First Responder Business Plus, Business Unlimited Ultimate+, Go5G Puerto Rico Business Plus, Go5G DHH Business Plus, Magenta®, Magenta® MAX, Magenta 55+, Magenta® MAX 55+, Magenta® First Responder, Magenta® MAX First Responder, Magenta® Military, Magenta® MAX Military, Magenta® Deaf or Hard of Hearing, Magenta® MAX Deaf or Hard of Hearing, Magenta® Amplified, Business Unlimited Select, Business Unlimited Advanced, Business Unlimited Ultimate, Magenta® for Business, and Magenta® MAX for Business rate plans. Simple Choice, Select Choice, and ONE plans are also included.

If you’re a T-Mobile customer on qualifying plan, you can add an International Pass to get more high-speed data and unlimited voice calling in 215+ countries and destinations.

International roaming is a service allowing you to continue using your mobile phone or other mobile device to browse the internet, as well as send and receive: emails, voice calls, and text messages while visiting another country.

Great news, while roaming internationally, you won't be charged for voicemails left in your inbox if your phone remains powered off or in airplane mode. However, you will be charged for the following:

In the US, several forms of testosterone are used for treatment, especially for conditions like hypogonadism. These include:

### 1. **Testosterone Cypionate** 
   - **Description**: A long-acting injectable ester of testosterone, commonly prescribed and available in the US.
   - **Pros**: 
     - Requires less frequent injections (typically every 1-2 weeks).
     - Provides stable testosterone levels for an extended period.
   - **Cons**: 
     - Levels can peak after injection and then gradually decline, potentially causing fluctuations.
     - May cause injection site pain or irritation.

### 2. **Testosterone Enanthate**
   - **Description**: Another long-acting ester similar to cypionate, widely used in both the US and worldwide.
   - **Pros**: 
     - Slightly faster onset compared to cypionate.
     - Commonly available and relatively affordable.
   - **Cons**: 
     - Requires injections every 1-2 weeks, with potential fluctuations in hormone levels.

### 3. **Testosterone Propionate**
   - **Description**: A short-acting ester that requires more frequent dosing.
   - **Pros**: 
     - Provides more stable hormone levels if administered frequently.
     - Rapid onset of action.
   - **Cons**: 
     - Requires injections every 2-3 days, which can be inconvenient.
     - More frequent injections may increase the risk of injection site pain.

### 4. **Testosterone Undecanoate (Aveed)**
   - **Description**: A very long-acting injectable, available in the US as Aveed, but more widely used outside the US.
   - **Pros**: 
     - Requires fewer injections (every 10-14 weeks), providing a more convenient treatment schedule.
     - Maintains more consistent testosterone levels.
   - **Cons**: 
     - More expensive than other options.
     - Can cause an oil embolism if injected improperly, though this is rare.

### 5. **Testosterone Suspension**
   - **Description**: Pure testosterone in a water base, without esters. It is less common and used primarily in bodybuilding rather than for medical therapy.
   - **Pros**: 
     - Fast-acting with no ester to delay absorption.
   - **Cons**: 
     - Requires daily or even multiple injections per day, making it impractical for long-term treatment.
     - Can cause significant pain at the injection site.

### Comparison Between the US and the Rest of the World:
- **Availability**: Testosterone cypionate and enanthate are widely available in both the US and internationally. Testosterone undecanoate is more commonly used in Europe and other countries outside the US but is available as Aveed in the US.
- **Regulations**: Different countries have varied regulations on the types and availability of testosterone preparations. For example, testosterone undecanoate is used more frequently outside the US due to its extended dosing interval.

The idea that testosterone cypionate causes more water retention than enanthate is largely anecdotal and not strongly supported by clinical evidence. Both cypionate and enanthate are very similar in their chemical structure and pharmacokinetics, with only slight differences in their ester chains, which result in almost identical absorption rates and half-lives (cypionate has a half-life of about 8 days, and enanthate about 7 days).

**Clinical Perspective:**
- There is no substantial clinical data that proves one ester causes more water retention than the other.
- Water retention, when it occurs, is more likely influenced by factors such as the dosage, individual response to testosterone, diet, activity level, and overall hormonal balance (e.g., levels of estradiol, which can rise with testosterone therapy and contribute to water retention).

**Anecdotal Observations:**
- Some users report experiencing more water retention with cypionate than with enanthate, but this is subjective and varies from person to person. These reports are often found in bodybuilding or hormone replacement therapy forums but lack rigorous scientific backing.

Overall, the likelihood of experiencing water retention depends more on the dose, frequency of injections, and individual physiology than on whether you are using cypionate or enanthate. Adjusting your dosage or managing estradiol levels (through lifestyle changes or medication) can help mitigate water retention if it becomes an issue.

### **Legal Considerations:**
1. **Controlled Substance Regulations**: In the US, testosterone is classified as a Schedule III controlled substance. It is illegal to import controlled substances without a valid prescription from a licensed US doctor, even if you obtain them legally abroad.
  
2. **Customs Regulations**: US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) prohibits the importation of prescription medications without a valid prescription from a US healthcare provider. Attempting to bring testosterone into the country without the proper documentation could lead to confiscation, fines, or legal action.

### **What You Can Do:**
- **Consult a Doctor in Panama**: You can see a doctor in Panama for a prescription, but this prescription will not be valid for importation into the US. However, you can legally use it while in Panama if needed.
  
- **Have Your US Doctor Prescribe It**: It’s safer to have your testosterone prescription filled in the US upon your return. If you explain your situation to your doctor, they may be willing to work with you to ensure you have adequate treatment during your trip.

### **Recommendation:**
- It’s best not to attempt to bring testosterone back to the US. Instead, maintain your treatment plan with your US doctor and pharmacy to avoid legal complications.

There is no significant medical reason preventing you from trying testosterone enanthate if you’re experiencing water retention with cypionate, especially since the two are very similar in their effects. Here’s what you should consider before making the switch:

### 1. **Similar Efficacy and Safety Profile**
   - Both cypionate and enanthate are long-acting esters, with enanthate requiring similar injection intervals (typically every 1-2 weeks).
   - They deliver nearly the same testosterone levels, so switching may not drastically change your overall experience.

### 2. **Potential Benefits of Trying Enanthate**
   - Some individuals report less water retention with enanthate, although this is anecdotal. Given that personal response to testosterone therapy varies, you might experience fewer side effects with enanthate.
   - If you want to experiment with a slightly different ester, enanthate is a logical alternative with a comparable safety and efficacy profile.

### 3. **Monitoring Estradiol Levels**
   - Water retention is often linked to increased estradiol (a form of estrogen) levels, which can rise with testosterone therapy. Regardless of whether you switch to enanthate or stay with cypionate, managing your estradiol levels through monitoring or medication (e.g., aromatase inhibitors) could reduce water retention.

### 4. **Consulting Your Doctor**
   - Before switching, discuss your concerns and experiences with your healthcare provider. They can help monitor your hormone levels, adjust dosing, or suggest other interventions that might mitigate water retention.

### 5. **Consistency and Adaptation**
   - Your body might take some time to adjust to the new ester. Monitor how you feel over the course of a few weeks to determine whether enanthate offers any noticeable differences.

Switching to enanthate is a reasonable step if you're looking to see if it alleviates your water retention. It’s important to track your response and consult your healthcare provider to ensure that the change is safe and effective. Adderall, like testosterone, is a controlled substance classified as Schedule II in the US, and bringing it into the country from abroad can be complicated, even with a prescription. Here’s what you should know:

### **Key Considerations for Adderall:**

1. **Strict Import Regulations**: Adderall is tightly regulated, and US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) does not allow the importation of Schedule II substances from another country, even if you have a valid US prescription.

2. **Purchasing in Panama**: Adderall is not commonly available in many countries outside the US, and the medication might be marketed under a different name or not available at all. Even if you find a similar amphetamine-based medication, it may not be identical in formulation or dosage.

3. **Documentation Requirements**: If you attempt to bring Adderall into the US:
   - Carry your original prescription with all necessary details (doctor’s contact information, DEA number, dosage).
   - Have a letter from your US doctor explaining your medical need and prescription.

4. **Declare the Medication**: If you bring any medication into the US, you must declare it to CBP officers upon entry.

### **Potential Risks**:
- **Confiscation**: Even with documentation, there is a high risk that Adderall will be confiscated at the border since importation of Schedule II substances is generally prohibited.
- **Legal Issues**: You could face fines or legal action if you attempt to import it without adhering to US regulations.

### **Best Practice**:
- **Obtain a 90-day supply from your US pharmacy** before traveling, if your insurance allows, or work with your doctor to ensure you have enough medication for your trip.
